quarterly_data.quarter: Cowboy Space press release: Getting Satellite Data to Earth Faster with NOAA (10-20-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Cowboy Space announced a cooperative research and development agreement (CRADA) with NOAA's National Environmental Satellite, Data, and Information Service (NESDIS) to test whether processing satellite data in space gets environmental information to Earth faster. Following the launch of its first satellite, Reason-1, the company is building Reason-2, which will carry its computing and data-processing payload when it launches in 2027; for that mission NOAA will provide an existing open-source AI model and historical raw VIIRS data, and Cowboy Space will run NOAA's Community Satellite Processing Package (CSPP LEO and MiRS) natively on NVIDIA GPUs in orbit. By pairing onboard processing with its own 25 Gbps optical terminal, the company aims to reduce total processing and downlink time for data collected in orbit by up to 125x (research test, not a commercial service).
quarterly_data.figure: Reason-2 launch in 2027; 25 Gbps optical terminal; up to 125x faster processing and downlink (aim)
